etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Middle French intégrité, from Latin integritās (“soundness, integrity”), from integer. Doublet of entirety.

definitions.definition: Steadfast adherence to a strict moral or ethical code.

quote.citation: 1613 (date written), William Shakespeare, [John Fletcher], “The Famous History of the Life of King Henry the Eight”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act V, scene i], lines 2920-2921:
quote.text: Stand up, good Canterbury: Thy truth and thy integrity is rooted  […]

quote.citation: 2023 June 22, Charles Hugh Smith, 2023-2030: Artifice Vs. Doom-Loops‎[1]:
quote.text: Living a lie saps us of integrity and moral cohesion to the point that we can no longer distinguish between the artifice being propped up and the real world.

definitions.definition: The state of being wholesome; unimpaired
The quality or condition of being complete; pure
(cryptography) With regards to data encryption, ensuring that information is not altered by unauthorized persons in a way that is not detectable by authorized users.
(aviation) The ability of systems to provide timely warnings to users when they should not be used for navigation.
